notes: Brackets are derived. The booklet prints no rate schedule: it prints the Nebraska Tax Table (PDF pages 46-49, 777 rows of 100 dollars from 60 to 77,760) and on page 49 a worksheet for income over 77,760. Page 14 says 'Electronic filers must use the Nebraska Tax Calculation Schedule', and that schedule is not in the sources. Only the top rate is printed: 5.20% (page 2; page 49 also '.0520'). The rates 2.46%, 3.51% and 5.01%, and every start above 0, are fitted.

How the fit was checked: every printed row of all four columns, 3,108 figures, is in brackets.derivation.table_rows at its midpoint, with the four worksheet amounts at 77,760, so the validator re-computes each one (its test is within 1 dollar). The stricter test used here was that the schedule at the midpoint, rounded to the dollar, equals the printed figure. It passes on every row and every worksheet amount, and the largest gap is under 0.50. The rows were parsed from one text layer and compared with the other: all 777 rows agree.

Bracket starts pinned by the table: with the four rates fixed, one whole-dollar value passes the rounding test: single and married filing separately 4,030 and 24,120; married filing jointly 8,040 and 48,250; head of household 7,510 and 38,590. On a grid of 0.01 percentage points, 2.46 and 3.51 are the only values that fit their bands in every column, and 5.01 is the only value that fits the third band in all three columns. The joint column has no full 5.20% band to test; 5.20% is the printed rate.

Bracket starts NOT pinned by the table: the start of the 5.20% band. The step from 5.01% to 5.20% is so small that a whole range passes the rounding test: single and married filing separately 38,793 to 38,897 (38,870 recorded); head of household 57,535 to 57,639 (57,630 recorded); married filing jointly 77,501 to 77,760 (77,760 recorded; the worksheet's 'over $77,760' is the top of this range, the rows alone would allow more). Treat these three figures as a place inside a range, not as the law's figure. The choice moves tax by at most 0.20 (single, separate, head of household) or 0.49 (joint) a year.

Page 49 prints one worksheet per status: (taxable income - $77,760) x .0520 + a constant of $3,566 (single and married filing separately), $3,088 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) or $3,276 (head of household). brackets.derivation.formula holds one constant tested against single and joint, and these as 'minus' figures are not printed, so it is left out (the format holds one formula constant, not one per status). The constants are table rows at income 77760 instead. The schedule stays within 0.45 of the worksheet at every income above 77,760: 0.45 under for single and married filing separately, 0.39 under for joint, 0.32 over for head of household.

The table's columns are Single, Married filing jointly, Married filing separately and Head of a household. The footnote reads 'A qualifying surviving spouse must also use this column' on the joint column, so qualifying surviving spouse has no key in brackets and uses married_joint. The married filing separately column equals the single column on all 777 rows. The table's first row is 60 to 160; nothing is printed under 60.

B's dependent entry moved with it.

Settlement 2026-11-07: who.basis on the military, CSRS and railroad reliefs: A said each_person, B said return; the booklet's tests are about each retiree's own service (page 26 'All military retirees'; page 27; page 24), so each_person under extraction brief rule 5. There is no age test or cap, so the tax is the same either way.

Settlement 2026-11-07: ne_csrs_annuity_exclusion: B listed 'Contributory plan' under other_conditions; page 27 prints no such test, so it is dropped. paying_states ['federal'] is added, because the line is limited to 'employment with the federal government' and public_pension alone would also read as a Nebraska state pension.

Settlement 2026-11-07: credit for the elderly or disabled: only B recorded it; kept, page 15 line 20 prints it. who.basis is return, not B's each_person: the line takes the return's federal credit. No amount is printed.

Settlement 2026-11-07: health insurance premiums for retired officers and firefighters: only B recorded it, with covers other_income; dropped as a relief and kept in the next note, because line 36 subtracts premiums paid, not any kind of income.

Settlement 2026-11-07: ne_federal_tax_liability_limit: neither reader recorded it; added after the check writer's review, because page 17 prints it and a low federal tax limits the Nebraska tax. Net adjustments under 5,000 include every negative figure, so a Social Security or military subtraction leaves the worksheet open.

Settlement 2026-11-07: ne_personal_exemption_credit: a separate return gets one credit, because line 4b is 'If your status is married, filing jointly' (page 12). Page 13's chart prints spouse boxes for married filing separately 'only if the primary taxpayer can claim a personal exemption for his or her spouse', which points the other way; line 4b is the direct instruction for the credit.

Settlement 2026-11-07: ne_earned_income_credit: neither reader recorded it as an entry; added, printed on page 18 line 44. credit_rate is a share of the federal credit, as cap_rule says, not of the income in covers.

Health insurance premiums paid by retired law enforcement officers and professional firefighters (Schedule I line 36, PDF page 27): a subtraction of the premiums for a retiree employed full time in such a post for at least 20 years and at least 60 years of age at the end of 2025, if the deduction did not reduce income on the federal return. No cap is printed.

Government pension of another state, including a New York State pension: not found in the booklet. Schedule I Part B and its instructions print no subtraction for one; 'public_pension_other_state' appears in no relief. The only subtraction for a non-military government pension is line 38, 'limited to' federal CSRS annuities. Not found in the booklet is what is recorded, not a statement that none exists; with no subtraction such a pension stays in federal AGI, where line 5 starts.
Nebraska state and local government pensions: not found in the booklet, same as above; line 38 is limited to federal employment.

Private pensions, IRA and 401(k) or other employer-plan distributions: no subtraction found. Page 13 line 5 lists 'retirement income (such as 401K distributions, pensions, etc.)' among income included in federal AGI, and no Schedule I line takes it out. Roth conversions and required minimum distributions: not mentioned in the booklet, Form 1040N or Schedule I (the words 'Conversion Chart' on pages 14 and 29 are about another state's return lines). Not found in the booklet.

Credit for tax paid to another state (line 19, Schedule II, PDF pages 14 and 29): a separate Schedule II for each state, 'The total credits cannot exceed the Nebraska tax liability'. It can apply to income another state taxes; it exempts no kind of income.

Nebraska other tax (line 16, PDF page 14): 29.6% of the federal tax on lump-sum distributions of qualified retirement plans and on early distributions of qualified retirement plans. The schema has no field for a tax figured on a federal tax; this is on top of the ordinary tax on the distribution.

Capital gains are otherwise taxed like other income: no separate rate found. The Special Capital Gains/Extraordinary Dividend Deduction (Schedule I line 19, PDF page 25) is 'available only to Nebraska residents, or partial-year resident while a resident' and its terms are in Form 4797N, which is not in the sources, so it is not recorded as an entry.

Indexing: the words inflation, indexed, adjusted annually and cost of living are not in the booklet or forms. One sentence still says the brackets are adjusted: PDF page 5, Employee Nebraska Wage Exclusion, the wage thresholds 'will be adjusted each tax year by the same percentage used to adjust the individual income tax brackets', so brackets is yes (2026-11-08); everything else is not_stated.
Surtaxes and recapture of the lower brackets: none found in the booklet.
Not recorded, not retirement or age based: the Relocation Incentive Act wage exclusion (line 42), college savings and Enable plan lines (20 to 22), and the other Schedule I lines.
Nonresidents and partial-year residents figure tax on Schedule III by a ratio of Nebraska income to total income, and take the personal exemption credit on Schedule III line 7.
